children: Bitcoin mining profitability is deteriorating. A recent drop in Bitcoin's price, combined with lower transaction-fee income, has left even the newest mining machines generating only a few dollars a day before electricity costs, according to estimates.

Crypto news outlet Bitcoin.com reported on November 22 that hashprice, a key measure of mining profitability, fell to $26.16 per PH/s per day on November 21. That marked the lowest level in recent years, according to Hashrate Index data. Hashprice refers to the mining revenue expected from a fixed amount of computing power.

Bitcoin fell as low as $55,081 this week before recovering the $59,000 level. Miner fee income, however, remains low. Over the past 24 hours, transaction fees accounted for just 0.64% of total block rewards.

Even the latest machines have limited profit potential once electricity costs are factored in. Assuming power costs of $0.10 per kilowatt-hour, the Bitmain Antminer S23 Hydro 3U is estimated to generate $6.29 a day. The Bitdeer Sealminer A4 Ultra Hydro was estimated at $4.92, while the Antminer S23 XP Hydro came in at $4.12. Those figures exclude additional costs such as equipment purchases and facility maintenance.

Kyle Chasse, founder of Master Ventures, wrote on X that Bitcoin's price had fallen below mining production costs. Miners now have to either shut down machines or sell coin holdings to cover operating expenses.

Despite weaker profitability, the network's total computing power has rebounded. Hashrate fell to 912 EH/s on November 14 before recovering recently to 1.065 ZH/s. Mining conditions improved in part after the previous difficulty adjustment reduced difficulty by 9.13%.

The next adjustment, due around November 27, could lift mining difficulty again. The current estimated increase is 8.99%. If difficulty rises, the amount of Bitcoin that can be mined with the same computing power declines. The final adjustment will depend on block production speed over the remaining period.

title: Bitcoin Mining Profitability Worsens as Hashprice Falls to $26 a PH/s
